facts.text: Ponce, founded August 12 1692, takes its name from Juan Ponce de León y Loayza, the great‑grandson of the famed conquistador.
In 2020, the National Trust for Historic Preservation listed Ponce’s Historic Zone among America’s most endangered historic places.
Along Calle 25 de Enero, Ponce’s red‑and‑black firefighter houses remain owned by descendants, offering a scenic glimpse into the city’s past.
The Museo de Arte de Ponce, opened in 1959 by Luis A., showcases Caribbean art and anchors the city’s cultural scene.
Every July, Ponce hosts a Bomba and Plena festival, where musicians parade through streets, celebrating the city’s vibrant Afro‑Puerto Rican rhythms.
In May, the Ponce Grand Prix draws over 100 track‑and‑field athletes, turning the city’s streets into a temporary stadium.
